item.title: Let's Walk!! Brookdale Park — Sat Nov 28, 9:30 AM
item.description:
Let's Walk!! If entering from Bellevue Avenue and park in the first parking lot on the left. We will be gathering near the playground area.
if entering from Watchung Ave, park and walk up to the upper parking lot near the playground area.
We will be walking the outer path. There are several break-off points if you do not want to walk the entire path.
The walk will be about an hour or at least 3-4 miles.
Wear comfortable shoes!
Please plan to arrive 5 minutes early. The walk will start promptly.
Brookdale Park offers the public access to both passive and active recreational activities as well as picturesque vistas. Trails for walking and running, lush groves and extensive lawns, playgrounds, sports fields, track facilities, tennis courts, an archery range and stadium grandstand are just some of the numerous attractions that make Brookdale Park a magnet for nature lovers, families, and physical fitness enthusiasts for miles around.

item.title: DETROIT JAZZ Documentary Screening at Montclair State University FREE 6PM W/FILMMAKERS — Mon Nov 30, 6:00 PM — Montclair State University Presentation Hall College of Communications and Media
item.description: Montclair State University’s College of Communications Film Forum and the Music Department present: A Film Screening of Emerita Professor Roberta Friedman’s the new feature documentary: The Best of the Best: Jazz from Detroit with Q&A w/Filmmakers Dan Loewenthal, Roberta Friedman, and writer Stryker Monday Night November 30th, 6PM-8:45PM. at College of Communication Building’s Presentation Hall. Synopsis: The Best of the Best: Jazz from Detroit chronicles the defining impact of Detroit’s innovative and influential jazz legacy and the iconic city that produced it. Inspired by Mark Stryker’s 2019 book, Jazz from Detroit, the 90-minute documentary weaves a compelling historical and cultural tapestry through the 20th and 21st centuries. Set within Detroit’s dramatic rise and fall as an industrial power and the struggles and triumphs of its creative and resilient African American community, the film connects the dots between the city’s history and Black musical excellence. Website: ht

item.description:
Tech Talks is a free informational series where library staff introduce and explain the technology topics that matter most in today's digital world. Each session takes a closer look at a new or complex topic—whether it's a trending app, an emerging technology, or a platform you've been hearing about but aren't quite sure how to navigate. Through demonstrations and clear, jargon-free explanations, you'll come away with a better understanding of the tech landscape around you. There's no hands-on component, so no devices are needed—just come ready to learn and ask questions.

item.title: DJ Rafe Gomez presents Danceteria REWIND at Porta — Sat Nov 28, 9:00 PM — Porta Montclair
item.description: DJ Rafe Gomez, host of the popular Twitch channel Danceteria REWIND, will present an immersive sonic and visual re-creation of the famed NYC nightclub Danceteria at Porta in Montclair. The free event, which will be the tri-state area’s official debut of Rafe’s multimedia performance, will take place on Saturday, 11/28, 499 Bloomfield Avenue, from 9pm to 1am. Danceteria was a New York hotspot from 1979 to 1986. It was famous for embracing iconic art (Keith Haring worked at the club as a waiter, Kenny Scharf was a member of the performance troupe, and Jean-Michel Basquiat painted murals), video, fashion, and music. It’s also where LL Cool J, the Beastie Boys, RuPaul, Debi Mazar, and Madonna got their starts. This year, Danceteria has been trending: Madonna released a #1 hit single titled “Danceteria” that chronicled her adventures there, and the UK synth duo Soft Cell’s new album “Danceteria” explores the early 80s downtown NYC scene that inspired their musical journey.
